newsitem.title: UK: Demand picks up for Latin American sugar freight.
newsitem.headline: Demand picks up for Latin American sugar freight.

text.p: Demand picked up on the Latin American sugar freight market on Monday after Thai shipments to Indonesia occupied centre stage for most of the past week, shipbrokers said.

Of the day's new inquiry, Genoc quoted for 14,000 tonnes in bags from Buenaventura to east Africa with options including Madagascar, Colombo, Red Sea, Pakistan and Bangladesh, for prompt onwards dates.
Louis Dreyfus was open for 21,000 tonnes min/max bulk sugar from Puerto Quetzal to US Gulf for 20/28 February and 14,300 tonnes in bags from Thailand to Indonesia.
Shipbrokers said Dreyfus also reissued an earlier order for 1,000 tonnes min/max bagged sugar from Odessa to Poti for 17/20 February.
Cuba continued to be popular as a quoted origin for bulk sugar into Europe and north Africa.
Vitol was open for 21,000 tonnes from the island to Morocco with Mediterranean, Egypt and Black Sea options for early February.
Pacol quoted for 14,500 tonnes to the Black Sea for the first half of February.
Shipbrokers said Benham's recent orders for both bagged and bulk sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Valparaiso and US Gulf were still open.
Shyvers Savoy issued an account order for 6/7,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from east coast Mexico to Merca for 20 Feb/10 March and also 12,000 tonnes in bulk from Reunion to Nantes for 1/5 March.
Another account order emerged from Allen Chartering, which quoted for 7,000 tonnes in bulk from Abidjan to US Gulf/Atlantic for 15/22 February.
Secretan was in the market with three bagged orders for February dates.

It quoted for a spot 6,500/13,000 tonnes from Rouen/Gdynia range to Mediterranean/Red Sea/Pakistan, 11,000 from Veracruz to Algeria with west/east Africa option for 10/20 February and 10/12,000 from east coast Mexico to east Africa for spot/prompt.
Shipbrokers said no new sugar fixtures had been reported.
